task.description: WF-03 Step 4 rework 2 of 3 for ISS-0446. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's re-gate (step-04b-test-design-validator-regate.json) FAILED with 1 MAJOR: the committed guard test's own comment claims it protects against reintroduction of the check-then-act pattern 'on top of it later,' but the validator measured (reintroducing the pattern at the real fix site, the neighboring test, leaving the guard untouched) only 2/15 (~13%) detection, and both catches came from the original probabilistic mechanism resurfacing in the mutated fix-site test itself, not from the guard. The coordinator directed the SECOND of the validator's two offered directions explicitly (narrow the claim, do not engineer a cross-test guard): rewrite the test's comment and the spec to state only what the test actually delivers (verifies this suite's own fetch_test_supervisor!/start_supervised! fixture idiom tears down cleanly under a widened window, in the abstract), judge whether the test's name should change, correct test/specs/ISS-0446.md without silently dropping the old claim, and state plainly what is NOT protected (a reintroduction at the fix site itself is not reliably caught by any test in this suite). Do not change the guard test's mechanics -- comment/name/doc and spec edits only. Do not touch lib/ or the fix.

result.summary:
AGREE WITH THE DIRECTION. Narrowing the claim is correct and building a cross-test guard would trade a real, already-diagnosed MAJOR (an overclaiming comment) for a speculative future one (a fragile test asserting something about a sibling test's implementation, structurally the same fragility class as the git-diff/git-history-dependent tests ISS-0378/ISS-0404/ISS-0413 already had to delete). I looked for a case that direction (a) clears that bar and did not find one worth making -- the guard test's own synthetic SlowTrapChild fixture is fundamentally decoupled from the fix site's real Poller-based fixture (different child module, different supervisor construction), so any cross-test guard would have to either (i) make the guard test inspect/instrument the neighboring test's source or runtime behavior directly (fragile, and exactly the git-diff-shaped fragility the precedent warns against), or (ii) duplicate the SlowTrapChild widening mechanism onto the REAL Poller's own child spec at the fix site -- which would require adding trap_exit/slow-terminate behavior to production code (Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller) purely to make a test fixture, a change to lib/ this rework is explicitly forbidden from making and which would also be a bad idea in its own right (the real Poller should not carry test-only trap_exit/sleep behavior). Neither option is worth pursuing.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED the validator's central measurement before touching anything, per this project's re-derive-don't-inherit rule: reintroduced the exact deleted Supervisor.start_link/2 + on_exit(fn -> if Process.alive?(sup_pid), do: Supervisor.stop(sup_pid) end) pattern at the real fix site (lines 1113-1134), leaving the new guard test (line ~1136) completely untouched. Ran the full file 5 times: 5/5 CLEAN ('Result: 43 passed' every time) -- the guard did NOT catch the reintroduced bug in any of my 5 runs, consistent with (and on the low end of, as expected for a small sample of a ~13%-per-run process) the validator's own 2/15 finding. Reverted via a pristine backup copy; SHA256 of the restored file (e34091b81d3eddf01b11553eeee7574a0a464c47fa5a6e15391347c2da3fc3f4) matched the pre-mutation hash exactly; git status --porcelain test/ lib/ empty afterward.

CHANGES MADE (comment/name/doc/spec only -- mechanics untouched, confirmed by diffing only comment blocks and moduledoc text, no assertion or call sequence changed):

1. test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs, the guard test's own name: changed from 'the ExUnit.fetch_test_supervisor!/0 + start_supervised!/1 fixture idiom above tears down cleanly even when the child's shutdown is slow (ISS-0446 regression guard)' to 'ExUnit.fetch_test_supervisor/0 + start_supervised!/1 (this suite's own throwaway-supervisor fixture idiom) tears down cleanly even when the child's shutdown is slow' -- dropped 'above' (which pointed at the neighboring test) and dropped '(ISS-0446 regression guard)' (which implied it guards the ISS-0446 fix site). The test still lives in the same describe block and its own body/assertions are byte-identical.

2. Rewrote the test's leading comment: kept the ISS-0446 background explanation (why the old pattern was a race) under a 'BACKGROUND' heading, then added a 'WHAT THIS TEST ACTUALLY VERIFIES, narrowed after measurement' section that explicitly states the test verifies only the fixture idiom's teardown behavior in the abstract, explicitly DENIES the old claim ('It does NOT verify... that nobody can reintroduce a check-then-act on_exit guard at the actual fix site... an earlier version of this comment claimed exactly that, and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR measured it false: ... only 2 of 15 attempts (~13%)... A reintroduction there is NOT reliably caught by this test, or by any other test in this suite'), and points to the spec for the residual-gap statement. Also softened the trailing in-body comment ('discriminates a regression in THIS FIXTURE IDIOM ITSELF... see the scope note above for what that does and does not cover') and the SlowTrapChild moduledoc (added an explicit paragraph: 'per that test's own corrected scope note, it does not guard against a reintroduction of the check-then-act pattern at the ISS-0446 fix site itself -- only against a teardown regression in this suite's fetch_test_supervisor/0 + start_supervised!/1 fixture idiom in the abstract'). Kept the module named Iss0446RegressionGuard.SlowTrapChild for historical/traceability reasons (documented explicitly in its own moduledoc why the name doesn't match its narrowed scope) rather than renaming it -- renaming touches more surface than the 'comment/name/doc changes only, do not destabilize mechanics' instruction intended, and the moduledoc now says plainly what the name does and doesn't mean.

3. test/specs/ISS-0446.md: added 'REVISION NOTE 2 (rework 2 of 3)' -- does NOT silently drop the prior claim, states it was 'measured false', quotes the validator's 2/15 figure and my own independent 0/5 spot-check, states the direction taken and why (narrow, don't engineer a cross-test guard, with the ISS-0378/0404/0413 fragility-precedent reasoning spelled out), and a dedicated 'The residual gap, stated plainly, not papered over' paragraph: a reintroduction AT THE FIX SITE is not reliably caught by this test or any other test in this suite; the only thing standing between a future edit and that regression is REVIEWER's structural argument plus ordinary code review, not automated coverage. Also corrected the 'Why this test' section's claim ('its violation is exactly what someone reintroduces... here later would look like' -> struck, replaced with an explicit pointer to REVISION NOTE 2 and an explicit denial), the 'What this proves' section (replaced the blanket claim with the measured ~13%/0-of-5 figures and a pointer to the residual-gap paragraph), and the coverage checklist's first line (now states the fix-site's real protection is REVIEWER's structural argument, not this test, and that (b) 'does NOT extend to reliably catching a reintroduction at the fix site').

DID NOT CHANGE: the test's assertions, call sequence, SlowTrapChild's actual behavior (trap_exit, Process.sleep(5), terminate/2), the describe block structure, or anything in lib/ or the ISS-0446 fix itself. Confirmed via git diff that only comment/moduledoc/string-literal-name lines changed in the .exs file.

RE-RAN AFTER EDITS, real output quoted:
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors: exit 0, zero output.
- mix format --check-formatted test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs: exit 0, zero output.
- mix test test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs -> 'Finished in 29.1 seconds (0.00s async, 29.1s sync)', 'Result: 43 passed'. Still green, same 43 tests as before this rework (mechanics unchanged, so no count change expected or observed).
- mix test test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs --only line:1136 (the guard test in isolation) -> 'Finished in 0.4 seconds (0.00s async, 0.4s sync)', 'Result: 1 passed, 42 excluded'. Still fast, still passes.

CLEANUP: pristine backup copy and all spot-check log files deleted after use. git status --porcelain (repo root) shows exactly two modified files: test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs and test/specs/ISS-0446.md. No scratch/ residue, no lib/ changes.
